properties.description: Forrest Gump (1994), directed by Robert Zemeckis and starring Tom Hanks, Robin Wright, and Gary Sinise, is a drama-romance that chronicles the life of a simple, good‑hearted man from Alabama as he drifts through defining moments of mid‑20th‑century America. Told through extended flashbacks, the film follows his episodic adventures—from childhood struggles to wartime experience and unexpected business ventures—while a lifelong longing for his childhood sweetheart shapes his journey. Blending whimsy, sentimentality, and historical montage, it examines themes of innocence, fate, perseverance, and the myths of the American Dream. The emotional tone balances warm nostalgia with poignant loss, anchored by a performance that emphasizes moral simplicity and resilience.
properties.plot_summary: Told in a series of flashbacks, an Alabama man with an intellectual disability narrates his unlikely life from childhood into adulthood. He drifts through pivotal moments of mid‑20th‑century America, finding unexpected success in a string of episodic adventures while never losing his longing for a childhood sweetheart. The story mixes whimsical episodes with bittersweet loss to examine innocence, chance, and perseverance against the backdrop of social change.

properties.description: The Big Lebowski (1998), directed by Joel and Ethan Coen, is a crime-inflected comedy starring Jeff Bridges, John Goodman, and Julianne Moore. A laid-back slacker is mistaken for a wealthy man and launches a quest to get restitution for his urinated-on rug, dragging his bowling buddies into a chaotic web of ransom plots, porn-industry figures, and eccentric criminals. The film blends deadpan humor, surreal set pieces, and noir tropes to examine themes of mistaken identity, nihilism, and fractured masculinity while cultivating a quotable, cult sensibility.
properties.plot_summary: A laid-back slacker is mistaken for a wealthy namesake and wakes up to find his rug soiled, setting him off on a bungled quest for restitution. He enlists his bowling buddies — an irascible Vietnam vet and a soft-spoken friend — and becomes entangled with kidnappers, porn-industry figures, and a group of nihilists. The supposed ransom scheme and a series of deceptions spiral into a chaotic, often surreal crime caper that resists tidy resolution.
